The configured dRPC endpoint alone did not provide these traces. BSC remained unavailable in the bounded probe; complete other-chain storage/archive capability and sustained outage recovery are not established. A direct public Gnosis historical-node opcode probe additionally succeeded: eth_chainId=100, debug_traceTransaction with full stack/storage and fresh canonical receipt. Its 236237-step trace normalizes 1354 reads and 186 writes across 519 verified frames. This is endpoint-specific evidence, not evidence that configured dRPC or every chain supports native opcode tracing. An alternate PublicNode BSC attempt stopped after one metered eth_chainId request with a legacy RuntimeError; chain identity, tracing and archive capability were not established. The old artifact lacks an HTTP status, which is not reconstructed. Offline diagnostics now retain a validated numeric HTTP status when available without leaking credential-bearing URLs, headers or bodies. This adds no successful BSC capture and does not broaden the claim. A separately preserved 2026-10-16 bounded retry with structured HTTP diagnostics received HTTP 403 for eth_chainId, then stopped after one metered request. No trace/receipt method was dispatched and no chain identity was established. This proves access denial for that request, not unsupported BSC tracing; the missing TRAIN trace and broader capability claim remain unverified. A further official-public-BSC capability probe confirmed chainID56 and then received JSON-RPC error code -32000 for debug_traceTransaction(callTracer) on the frozen TRAIN Fortress transaction. It stopped immediately after2meteredrequests; no trace body was accepted and no subsequent method dispatched. The raw provider message was not retained, so this establishes rejection of that specific historical trace request, not that the method is universally unsupported, nor an archive-capability explanation. Receipt/basic-read success from prior evidence does not imply historical debug support.
